title: The Span of Medical Plan Bills Read When Rider Arrears are Settled
content:
The money left over on the medical plan bill is a figure taken from the member's Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment — the premium charges and premium payments booked on that enrollment's own premium account. Which of those bills are read, when arrears on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders are settled, follows from the standing of that enrollment and the day the rider took effect.

## The rule

**Where the medical plan enrollment the rider hangs on does not stand in force and carries a day its coverage ended**, the money left over is taken over the bills raised up to that day.

**Where that enrollment stands in force and the rider took effect after it did**, the money left over is taken over the bills raised from the day the rider took effect to the handling date.

**Otherwise**, the money left over is taken over every bill raised on that medical plan enrollment.

## Condition, judgement, span

| What the Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment shows | The span read |
|---|---|
| Not in force, and carrying a day its coverage ended | The bills raised up to that day |
| In force, and the rider took effect after the enrollment did | The bills raised from the day the rider took effect to the handling date |
| In force, and the rider took effect no later than the enrollment did | Every bill raised on that enrollment |
| Not in force, but carrying no day its coverage ended | Every bill raised on that enrollment |

## What is read over the span

Over whichever span governs, two sums are taken from that enrollment's premium entries: what has been paid on the bills, and the medical plan premium charged on them. The money left over is the first less the second, taken over the same span and never less than nothing.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

A Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment stands in force. Its premium account carries charges of 42.00 USD in each of six successive calendar months and payments of 42.00 USD in five of them and 120.00 USD in the sixth. The rider took effect at the start of the fifth of those months.

Because the enrollment stands in force and the rider took effect after it did, the span read is the bills raised from the day the rider took effect to the handling date: the fifth and sixth months. Over that span 162.00 USD has been paid and 84.00 USD charged, and the money left over is 78.00 USD.

Had the enrollment ceased to stand in force and carried a day its coverage ended in the fourth month, the span read would instead have been the bills raised up to that day.
